rationale: G2's round-4 ask is ADDRESSED: the audit now records the accepted identity, automatic reads require audit tuple == binding == independently scanned candidate, and AC-11 pins the M1-to-M2 stale-audit composition. However, the new F2 rule mistakes panel-local round numbers for chronology across independent registration directories. A scratch real-git probe, using the actual panel.Create/Scan/ForBead functions and a literal model of the proposed F2 predicate, accepts a later, visible, unlanded review at a new panel's default round 1 when an older landed panel is at round 5. Changing only the newer panel's local counter to 6 makes it refuse. A genuine previously accepted tuple would therefore remain usable after that newer review, despite rerunning F2. This is an ordinary writer-composition fail-open, not a request to authenticate agent-writable state. Thirteen existing lifecycle trust tests passed; spec validation exited 0 with one missing-epic warning. This verdict reviews the specification at 7404845f, not a future implementation. All mutations were confined to the scratch clone and its throwaway repositories.
concrete_changes_required: G2r5.1: Replace R4.2(F2)'s comparison of every non-ancestor registration's round against the maximum anchor round with an ordering rule grounded in the panel writer's actual contract. Round is local to a panel, defaults to 1 for a new slug, and has no enforced bead-wide sequence relationship across directories. A non-ancestor registration must not be dismissed as earlier solely because its integer is smaller than an unrelated anchor's integer. Establish and validate an explicit ordering relationship before allowing the rebased-away-earlier exception; otherwise refuse fail-closed as incomparable, naming the existing override/attested-restore exits. Keep the equal-or-ancestor anchor needed for the tree-identical complete wrapper. Extend AC-11 for both reattest and automatic read-back: old panel A at round 5 lands; a genuinely later new panel for the same bead registers unlanded B at its default round 1; bead/X is absent or reset. Both acceptance and read-back must refuse, including read-back with an already genuine matching audited tuple. Pin that changing only the new panel's local counter cannot turn the refusal into acceptance. Retain a positive earlier-rebased-round fixture only where the revised contract can actually establish its ordering. Update the ADR-0041 amendment contract, visibility wording and bounded-reach claim consistently. This can remain a caller-side conservative rule and does not require signatures, a trusted store, or general panel-substrate redesign.

findings.title: Round-4 ask status
findings.detail: G2r4.1 — ADDRESSED. spec.md:420-430 adds accepted merge SHA and second-parent audit keys beside scanned_branch, writes them with the binding, requires tuple equality with both the current binding and the independently scan-derived candidate, and reruns F1-F5 on read-back. The stale genuine audit after an ordinary executor MergeMetadata rewrite grants nothing under that equality test. AC-11(xii) now explicitly exercises real reattest of M1, executor rewrite to M2 retaining the M1 audit, automatic refusal, and a fresh multiple-candidate refusal with no write. AC-11(xi) preserves the audit-on-unchanged-binding write; (i-r) preserves the valid same-tuple no-op. AC-18 pins the amended ADR contract. None of G2's round-4 required changes is PARTIAL or MISSED. G2r5.1 is a NEW_ISSUE in this round's replacement F2 rule.

findings.title: Panel-local round counters can hide a genuinely later unlanded review
findings.detail: spec.md:404-409 treats a non-ancestor review with round less than the maximum anchor round as historical and harmless. But internal/panel/create.go:64-65 defines a panel round, Create copies the supplied round into that directory without consulting other panels, cmd/mindspec/panel.go:329 defaults it to 1, and plugins/mindspec/skills/ms-panel-run/SKILL.md:28-30 likewise exposes a slug and a default-1 panel round. Co-writing round and reviewed_head_sha prevents drift within a write; it does not establish chronology between slugs. The scratch probe TestG2Round5IndependentPanelCounters creates old-review at round 5 on landed A, then new-review at round 1 on genuinely later B, for the same bead. B is outside the tip's history; both registrations are visible through the real Scan/ForBead. The real #239 topology has exactly one admitted off-first-parent landing, no surviving bead branch, and gitutil.ContentSubsumedOutcome confirms its content remains landed. The literal new F2 predicate nevertheless PASSES. Keeping the graph, registrations and B unchanged while changing new-review's counter to 6 makes it refuse. Thus a previously genuine matching audit is not invalidated by this later review, and a fresh fallback reattest would also pass the proposed checks. No forged SHA, fabricated merge, malformed record, or deliberate audit forgery is needed. Evidence: round-rule-probe.json and repo/internal/lifecycle/g2_round5_probe_test.go in this scratch directory. The predicate is explicitly modeled because the proposed fallback/F2 implementation does not exist at the reviewed commit. The current ACs only use conveniently increasing counters and miss the incomparable-panel case.

findings.title: The audited tuple bounds identity reuse but does not authenticate an operator
findings.detail: A bd writer can still fabricate both the binding and every audit key in one metadata update; actor, op and timestamp are shape checks, not authentication. The new accepted-pair equality correctly prevents an authentic old audit from accidentally attaching to a different merge. Re-running candidate count, surviving-tip and current-tip content checks prevents metadata alone from bypassing those git facts. The specification now honestly states the new bounded acceptance of an undirected off-first-parent merge and the loss of the operator-vouch distinction under deliberate forgery. Evidence-file hashes similarly bind bytes, not truth or human approval. A repository writer can forge panel registrations, and a history writer can spoof merge subjects. ADR-0037 section 8 explicitly excludes anti-adversary authentication at this layer; no such mechanism is requested. The high finding concerns honest panel writes and their incomparable counters, rather than those accepted deliberate-forgery residuals.

findings.title: Ancestor anchors and PlanMapsBead retain their intended structural boundaries
findings.detail: The equal-or-ancestor anchor is not itself ancestor-tolerant landed-identity confirmation. If the candidate's second parent is reachable from the tip, any SHA genuinely ancestral to it is also reachable by transitivity; an actually unlanded SHA cannot masquerade as such an ancestor without changing the graph or the registration's SHA. The tree-identical complete wrapper therefore justifies allowing an ancestor anchor, while F2 still needs a sound ordering relation between registrations. PlanMapsBead now requires both the Nth positional Bead heading and work_chunks id N, matching the existing section extractor and MF-1 structural inputs; half-mapping does not confer selectable membership. Plan content remains repository-writable, and remaining content failures stay in MF-1. metadata.spec_id remains a near-miss link rather than claim membership; R1.8 retains lineage/spec checks, and lineage-less N4 cannot use a readiness override. I established no additional selection fail-open from this round's mapping changes.

findings.title: Verification and scope
findings.detail: The scratch F2 probe passed and produced round-rule-probe.json. Thirteen existing lifecycle tests passed, covering forged bindings without real merges, bindings at another bead's merge, anonymous and unrecognized subjects, inconsistent binding pairs (both subcases), the primary-path happy/no-op path, a surviving-tip contradiction, audited contradictory-binding repair, true and masked reverts, and stale-older-remerge repair. These exercise existing primitives, not a shipped fallback, audited-tuple validator or PlanMapsBead implementation. Running go run ./cmd/mindspec validate spec 129-readiness-tracker-honesty in the clone exited 0 and printed: '129-readiness-tracker-honesty: 1 issue(s) found' followed by '[WARN] lifecycle-binding: spec has no beads epic; run spec approve to create one'. I did not run the suggested lifecycle mutation. The source repository and clone both resolve to reviewed commit 7404845f401f4839d4ddec0ce3969d65ac9270fe; source repository writes were not performed.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: Round-5 summary B's unconditional wording that F2 fails closed on 'no anchor' overstates spec.md:407: no anchor refuses only while a non-ancestor registration exists; no registrations therefore does not itself refuse. More substantively, the brief/consolidation's description of ordering by round inherits the unsupported assumption that counters from separate registration dirs provide chronology; G2r5.1 demonstrates the error in that assumption. The generic reviewer-conduct example git worktree add would write administrative data in the source repository despite the read-only instruction; I used the user-authorized no-hardlinks scratch clone instead. The prior-round O3/F1 lens discrepancies are corrected in the current lens table, and historical round sections are explicitly historical. The header destination is expressly overridden later and by the user's verdict.json instruction, so that is not an unresolved destination error.
